nodes.label: AuthNav
nodes.rationale: Client-side optimistic auth slot for the Navbar; deliberately not the source of truth for access control -- (protected)/layout.tsx's server-side session recheck is.

nodes.label: Lighthouse CI as report-only, not a merge gate (rationale)
nodes.norm_label: lighthouse ci as report-only, not a merge gate (rationale)

nodes.label: LanguageProvider
nodes.rationale: Initial render uses project.config.json's defaultLanguage; cookie is checked post-mount to avoid a blank-page flash.

nodes.label: COOKIE_NAME
nodes.rationale: Kept in a client-free file because a named export from a 'use client' module can't be imported into a Server Component -- RSC wraps every export as a client reference, which throws when read on the server.

nodes.label: LegalTranslation
nodes.rationale: Real substantive legal copy (not Lorem Ipsum), genericized for any app built from this template. 'LPJ IT-Solutions' operator name stays a literal placeholder string, not interpolated. Imprint address/email stay bracketed TODOs since a template can't invent legally required real facts.

nodes.label: buildAdminNotificationEmail
nodes.rationale: Built as a real <table> (not flexbox/grid) so pasting it out of the mail client into Excel/Sheets keeps rows intact.

nodes.label: buildConfirmationEmail
nodes.rationale: Hardcoded German, independent of defaultLanguage -- no i18n system exists yet for contact-form email content.

nodes.label: createJsonLd
nodes.rationale: Defaults type to 'WebSite' since this template ships marketing/account pages, not articles; pass type:'BlogPosting' explicitly for a future article page.

nodes.label: createNoIndexMetadata
nodes.rationale: For pages behind auth: no OG/Twitter/canonical, just a title and hard noindex -- nothing there is meant to be publicly discoverable.

nodes.label: createSiteMetadata
nodes.rationale: A page exporting its own openGraph object doesn't automatically inherit opengraph-image.tsx's file-convention image -- Next only falls back when a segment defines no openGraph metadata at all, so the fallback to /opengraph-image is made explicit here.

nodes.label: POST /api/contact route
nodes.rationale: Responds 503 if CONTACT_SMTP_*/CONTACT_TO_EMAIL are unset -- fails closed rather than a silent no-op.

nodes.label: Dynamic rendering for per-request CSP nonce
nodes.rationale: Pages with no other dynamic data must still call connection() to force dynamic rendering, or Next prerenders them statically and strict-dynamic blocks their scripts in production since no request/nonce is available at build time.
nodes.norm_label: dynamic rendering for per-request csp nonce

nodes.label: Optimistic-only client auth check principle
nodes.rationale: Client/middleware-level auth checks only decide what to optimistically show; server-side re-checks remain the actual access-control source of truth.

nodes.label: {{appName}} interpolation mechanism
nodes.rationale: t(key, params?) replaces {{paramName}} tokens with data instead of hardcoding strings; appName from project.config.json is always available, an explicit params.appName (e.g. backend welcome notification) overrides it per call.

nodes.label: ADR-007: static prerender via CSP hash reverted
nodes.rationale: An attempt to statically prerender no-per-request-content pages via hash-based CSP ('sha256-...' instead of 'nonce-...') was reverted after a real production build showed it breaks hydration -- Next's own per-page inline RSC hydration payload (self.__next_f.push) can't be hand-hashed and has no nonce on a static page.
nodes.norm_label: adr-007: static prerender via csp hash reverted

nodes.label: CSP nonce requirement for JSON-LD script tags
nodes.rationale: Every page rendering <JsonLd> must pass the request's CSP nonce or the browser silently drops the <script type=application/ld+json> tag; this was previously broken (no nonce passed) before being fixed.
nodes.norm_label: csp nonce requirement for json-ld script tags

nodes.label: cid: logo attachment mechanism for email
nodes.rationale: Logo is embedded as a cid: attachment rather than inlined base64 or a bare hosted URL because cid is the option that reliably renders across mail clients without depending on the app being deployed/reachable.
nodes.norm_label: cid: logo attachment mechanism for email
